o: Starting at room j with hp, after entering room i your health is hp − (damage[1] + … + damage[i]). Room i earns a point iff hp − D[i] ≥ requirement[i], where D is the damage prefix sum. Crucially, whether room i scores does not depend on the starting room j — only on i! So score(j) is just the number of scoring rooms i ≥ j, computable with a suffix-count array. Total = Σ score(j) = Σ over scoring rooms of (number of starts ≤ i) — one linear pass.
k: Room i's point condition depends only on i, not on the starting room — decouple and use suffix counts.

a.i: Mark good[i] = (hp - D[i] >= req[i]); suffix sums S[j] = #{good i ≥ j} = score(j); answer = Σ S[j]. Equivalently each good room i contributes (i) starts (1-indexed rooms 1..i), i.e., answer = Σ i·good[i] with 1-indexed i.
s: Answer = Σ (i+1) over 0-indexed good rooms (each good room i serves starts 0..i, that's i+1 starts).
a.t: O(n) — single pass with running damage

a.i: Build good[] booleans, then suffix sums S where S[j] = score(j), and sum them. More explicit, easier to explain, same complexity.
s: D = prefix damages; good[i] = hp - D[i] >= req[i].

w: The insight that scoring is start-independent collapses an O(n²) simulation into O(n). Verify on sample 1: good rooms are 1 and 2, contributing 1 + 2 = 3. Watch overflow: answer up to ~n²/2 = 5·10⁹, use 64-bit. Follow-up: what if hp regenerates or requirements depend on the path?
